HYPOTHESIS: The repair loop is not caused by an unlocated defect. It is caused by the routing key of the finding. .opencode/scripts/route-wave-findings.py resolves a finding's execution owner from (a) the frontmatter owner index, keyed by the requirement IDs appearing in the finding text, and (b) infer_lifecycle_owner at lines 187-193, which falls back to a Wave whose ID prefixes the finding_id. Dispatch 163 delivered the corrected finding as 'W57-PKGREG-SHELL-CLOSE-HIDE-DEADLOCK' with no cited requirement row, so both routes fail and the router returns the reporting Wave. Measured proof: the identical finding text routes to execution_owner=W57, owner_state=pending without a cited requirement row, and to execution_owner=W55, owner_state=done for the same defect as soon as the owning requirement row is cited. The controller therefore never received a routable W55 row and re-dispatched W57, which is exactly the observed no-progress cycle.

No file under src/, tests/, scripts/, build/ or waves/ was modified. The frozen candidate was not rebuilt or patched. No acceptance gate was redefined. No test was weakened, skipped or xfailed. No file under .opencode/ was modified.
RESULT: HYPOTHESIS CONFIRMED. (1) Dispatch 163's claim that REQUIREMENT_REGISTRY.md and TODO_OWNERSHIP_MAP.md are 'absent from the repository' is FALSIFIED; both exist under opencode/ and dispatch 163's residual gap is therefore not a controller-owned blocker, it was a search miss. (2) The owning requirement row for the embedded-WebView2 shutdown deadlock is machine-resolved as HPC-W10-GJ2-051, MANDATORY, 'Workstream A3 - Resource/lifecycle soak', wording 'WebViews;', registry Owning Wave W55, confirmed by waves/done/W55.md frontmatter which lists HPC-W10-GJ2-024..054. (3) Dispatch 163's cited rows are semantically wrong even though its Wave-level route was directionally right: the registry defines HPC-W10-GJ2-029 as 'keyboard accelerators;', HPC-W10-GJ2-030 as 'status bar/connection indicator;' and HPC-W10-GJ2-038 as 'keyboard-only traversal for core journey;'. None of them is a WebView or lifecycle requirement. (4) The maintained router now emits execution_owner=W55, owner_state=done for HPC-W10-GJ2-051 from a plain phase-result, so the closed-owner transaction is deliverable rather than inferred. (5) A second real product defect was surfaced for the first time: pty_resize=FAIL, whose owning row machine-resolves to HPC-W05-TERM-023, MANDATORY, 'Workstream F - Resize', wording 'window/widget resize updates PTY size;', Owning Wave W20 (CLOSED). It was never routed because the gate's timed_out branch discarded the runtime evidence that records it. W57's blocker is therefore two owned-Wave defects, not one.
